questions.question: Does Cursor work well on large, existing codebases?
questions.answer_summary: Cursor's automatic embedding-based retrieval works well when it successfully pulls the right files into context, but reviewers report it starts hallucinating more on large monorepos or fragmented codebases when it can't.

questions.question: How does Claude Code's context window compare to Cursor's on big codebases?
questions.answer_summary: Comparisons describe Claude Code offering a much larger context window (reported up to roughly 1M tokens in some configurations) versus Cursor's typical 128K-256K token range.

questions.question: Why do AI coding agents perform better on greenfield projects than on legacy ones?
questions.answer_summary: Greenfield projects have no history, no hidden dependencies, and explicit, visible conventions, whereas legacy systems have real constraints scattered across incident postmortems, Slack threads, and undocumented institutional memory.

questions.question: Can AI coding agents actually do better on legacy code in some respects?
questions.answer_summary: Counterintuitively, yes in some ways — legacy systems often come with years of accumulated documentation, runbooks, and postmortems that a brand-new greenfield project simply doesn't have yet.

questions.question: What's the biggest risk of using AI coding agents on brownfield/production codebases?
questions.answer_summary: AI agents can produce plausible-looking, syntactically valid, but semantically wrong changes that slip through code review and reach production, which is especially costly in regulated domains like insurance, banking, or healthcare.

questions.question: Why does code review sometimes fail to catch AI-generated bugs in legacy systems?
questions.answer_summary: Reviewers depend on contextual familiarity with the codebase that the AI agent doesn't have, and that context is often scattered across undocumented institutional knowledge rather than in the code itself.

questions.question: What workflow do experienced developers use to combine these tools?
questions.answer_summary: A commonly cited hybrid pattern is using Cursor or Copilot for day-to-day editing and Claude Code for more complex, large-context or agentic tasks.

questions.question: How should teams do context engineering for AI agents working on legacy codebases?
questions.answer_summary: Guides recommend feeding agents accumulated context such as runbooks and postmortems, and using scoped instruction/rule files, as part of a documented set of fixes for legacy-code context gaps.

questions.question: Is it safe to "vibe code" a greenfield project?
questions.answer_summary: It's considered lower-risk on greenfield projects because there are no real users yet to be harmed by mistakes, though quality standards are expected to rise once users arrive.

questions.question: What does GitHub Copilot lack compared to Claude Code or Cursor for large-codebase understanding?
questions.answer_summary: Comparative reviews describe Copilot as lacking Claude Code's large context window and Cursor's codebase-embedding/composer-level understanding.

questions.question: Why is verification cost framed as lower than production-bug cost when using AI agents on brownfield systems?
questions.answer_summary: The argument made is that investing time in verifying AI-authored changes costs far less than the cost of an AI-introduced bug reaching production in a high-stakes brownfield system.

questions.question: Do experts see more risk or more speed benefit from AI coding assistants overall?
questions.answer_summary: Industry commentary frames it as a speed-vs-risk tradeoff that experts weigh differently depending on codebase maturity and domain criticality.
